audit_notes: Critical checks: (1) Actuation direction: pine-cone scales open when dry; the laminate must be arranged so that dry air closes the flaps. In hot-dry climates daytime RH 10-20 percent and night 30-50 percent gives a usable RH swing, but in hot-humid climates the swing is small. (2) Durability: cellulose-based hygromorphs lose 30-60 percent of their curvature amplitude after a few years of UV and wetting; a 20-year mean actuation availability of ~0.6 is optimistic. (3) Flap temperature: 15 cm flaps have h ~10 W/m2K per side, so an aged flap (alpha ~0.4) runs ~6 K above air and radiates toward the wall. Bimorph curvature (Timoshenko, equal thickness and modulus): kappa = 1.5*d_eps/t = 1.5*0.02*0.3/0.002 = 4.5 1/m for a 30 percent RH swing, i.e. tip rotation over 0.15 m ~ 0.68 rad - enough to close. Dimensionless: flap Reynolds number 2*0.15/1.6e-5 = 1.9e4; Biot envelope 0.035. Model: steady 1D wall conduction with a shaded outer boundary; audited actuation_availability 0.6, flap_solar_absorptance 0.4. Baseline: exposed wall with aged cool paint (h_o 20, no flaps). Expected gain only ~2 percent: the sheltered wall loses convective cooling and the warm flaps re-radiate, which nearly cancels the shading of an already white wall. Simulation coefficient: bilayer curvature 4.5 1/m. Mechanical: flap hinges and wind flutter over 20 years are a concern. Audit passed.
